memory_leads.lead: Shipboard habitability is a coupled operating system rather than an amenity list. Sleeping spaces, food and water, sanitation, ventilation and thermal conditions, noise/vibration, lighting, work-space ergonomics and common spaces jointly determine whether a crew can recover and sustain safe work over long tours.

Sleeping accommodation is recovery capacity. Berth privacy, motion/noise transmission, temperature, ventilation, light control and interruptions can reduce effective rest even when nominal off-duty hours exist, so rest opportunity and rest quality should be represented separately.

Noise and vibration propagate through both work and rest states. Machinery, propeller/hull excitation, ventilation equipment, alarms, maintenance and cargo activity can create persistent background load that affects communication, concentration and sleep without necessarily appearing as a discrete casualty.

Ventilation, heating/cooling and humidity control are continuous habitability services. Their adequacy varies by climate, machinery load, occupancy and equipment condition; degraded thermal or air-quality conditions can accumulate fatigue and maintenance burden before becoming an obvious operational failure.

Potable-water availability is a chain from bunkering or production through treatment, storage, distribution and point-of-use access. Quantity, continuity and quality are distinct states, and a local tank, pump, treatment or contamination problem can constrain habitability even when total water inventory appears sufficient.

Food service is a logistics-and-production chain: procurement/provisioning, storage, inventory rotation, galley preparation, dietary suitability and palatability all matter. Long voyages or disrupted resupply can turn food quality and variety into morale and retention factors even without a formal shortage.

Sanitation and hygiene depend on functioning toilets/showers, drainage, sewage handling, cleaning, laundry, waste management and consumables. Degradation in one service can spread workload to housekeeping or maintenance and reduce recovery quality without immediately reducing navigational capability.

Lighting has both task and recovery roles. Work areas need sufficient, reliable illumination for inspection and manual tasks, while accommodation benefits from controllable darkness and day/night cues; outages, glare or inappropriate lighting can therefore affect both error risk and sleep quality.

Ergonomics is embedded in ship layout and task design: access, ladder/stair geometry, reach, posture, lifting, tool use, control placement and maintenance clearances influence workload and injury exposure. A technically operable system can still impose recurring human burden through poor access or awkward manual work.

Mess rooms, recreation rooms, gyms, open-deck access and other common spaces can provide social and psychological recovery distinct from sleep. Their availability, condition and actual usability matter more than nominal presence, especially on long tours with limited shore access.

Habitability has its own maintenance backlog. HVAC, plumbing, refrigeration, galley, laundry, accommodation fixtures and insulation/acoustic treatments compete for technical attention and spares; deferred minor defects can compound into persistent living-condition degradation and extra crew workload.

Occupancy and service demand matter independently of certified accommodation capacity. Riding squads, trainees, contractors, supernumeraries or temporary staffing can increase demand on berths, sanitary systems, food, water and common spaces, changing habitability without changing the vessel's physical plant.

Spatial separation from machinery, cargo hazards, heat sources and vibration paths is part of habitability design. The same ship can expose different crew groups to different environmental loads depending on cabin/workplace location and duty pattern, so vessel-wide averages can hide role-specific experience.

P032 fatigue is refined because formal rest hours do not equal restorative recovery. Replay should separate off-duty time from the environmental conditions that make sleep and decompression actually possible.

P033 employment/welfare and retention are refined because living conditions are part of the experienced employment package. Crew may evaluate tour length, employer quality and willingness to return partly through recurring accommodation, food and connectivity-to-common-space conditions rather than wage alone.

P036 occupational-health readiness is refined by separating the upstream physical environment from downstream illness/injury response. Heat, noise, vibration, sanitation and ergonomics are prevention/exposure states; medical care is a later response layer.

P028 electrical availability is refined because hotel loads such as ventilation, lighting, pumps, refrigeration and water services can lose habitability function before or after propulsion-related functions, creating a human-endurance dimension to degraded-power operation.
The atlas already notes labor/crewing as under-recalled negative space; P037 adds concrete living/work-environment states rather than repeating the broad coverage limitation.

Generic known-time, temporal precision and Memory-not-Evidence boundaries are already Baseline semantics; P037 applies them to habitability states whose exact onset or severity may only be known after inspection or complaint.

reviewed_no_specific_memory.reason: Exact standards, measurement methods, thresholds and historical implementation vary by vessel, flag, build date and jurisdiction and require dated Evidence.
Blind memory supports structural states but not claim-scoped vessel conditions, inspection outcomes, complaint histories or causal findings.
Provider lineages and capabilities are directory-like and recall-biased; exact identities and performance require source-first research.
Current conditions and individual experiences are time-sensitive and require contemporaneous source Evidence rather than blind recall.

stop_reason: The physical living/work-environment chain is populated from sleep/accommodation through noise/vibration, thermal/ventilation, food/water, sanitation, lighting/ergonomics, common-space recovery and maintenance/occupancy coupling. Further recall becomes standard-, measurement-, vessel-, supplier-, inspection-, complaint- or jurisdiction-specific.
truth_boundary: Memory-only orientation; no vessel habitability compliance, environmental measurement, food/water quality, health effect, crew complaint, supplier capability or current living condition is verified.
